teams.heading: Joji Nasova stays with Fijian Drua as Newcastle transfer is cancelled
teams.body: Fijian wing Joji Nasova will remain with the Fijian Drua after his planned transfer to Premiership side Newcastle Red Bulls was cancelled. The 25-year-old Olympic silver medallist had agreed to join the English club, but he has been released from his contract due to undisclosed personal reasons. Newcastle general manager Neil McIlroy confirmed the decision, stating: "While we were very much looking forward to welcoming Joji to Newcastle Red Bulls, we fully understand and respect the unique personal circumstances that have led to this decision."

lead.why: Fijian wing Joji Nasova's highly anticipated move to Premiership club Newcastle Red Bulls has been cancelled for personal reasons, keeping him in Fiji.

teams.heading: Ellis Genge delivers expletive-laden speech as footage reveals England dressing room details
teams.body: Newly released footage from the O2 Inside Line series has captured vice-captain Ellis Genge delivering a fiery, expletive-laden pre-match address before the recent victory in Santiago del Estero. Genge urged his teammates to 'cause some pain' following the football team’s World Cup semi-final exit, a motivation that preceded a chaotic encounter featuring four overlapping England yellow cards. Despite the disciplinary lapses, the squad survived a frantic final TMO decision to secure a 31-24 win, leaving Steve Borthwick’s side fourth in the Nations Championship standings.

teams.heading: Matt Williams slams Ireland as failing to meet elite test standards
teams.body: Former coach Matt Williams has labelled Ireland's recent Nations Championship performances as "well below elite standards," following the team's error-strewn 40-21 defeat to New Zealand. Williams criticised the side for a lack of defensive intensity and technical accuracy throughout the July window, pointing to 18 turnovers and 35 missed tackles in the final fixture at Eden Park. Head coach Andy Farrell acknowledged the team's shortcomings, stating, "Inaccurate is the word," while promising a period of reassessment after a difficult campaign.

teams.heading: Italy Record Rankings Throughout The Nation's Participation In Men's Rugby
teams.body: Italy has reached a peak of No. 8 in the World Rugby rankings during two distinct windows in their history. The side first achieved this position in 2007, marking a high point for the nation during that year’s international cycle. The Azzurri subsequently returned to the No. 8 spot in 2024. These two periods represent the highest world ranking the team has achieved since the current iteration of the official classification system was established.

teams.heading: Nigel Owens criticises Tomás Albornoz following misconduct charges after England match
teams.body: Former referee Nigel Owens has condemned the conduct of Tomás Albornoz and Pumas supporters following the narrow loss to England. Albornoz faces misconduct charges from World Rugby after remonstrating with official Angus Gardner at the final whistle. Owens labelled the player's behaviour and the subsequent abuse directed at match officials as "totally, totally unacceptable," insisting that such actions have no place in the sport. The incident followed a controversial TMO decision that denied Argentina a potential match-tying try.

teams.body: New head coach Les Kiss has signalled a fresh start by recalling powerhouse Lukhan Salakaia-Loto in his first 34-man squad. Following a "robust conversation" with his coaching staff, Kiss emphasised that no positions are guaranteed as he begins preparations for next month’s Japan series. While the squad retains captain Harry Wilson and core talent, veteran prop James Slipper has been rested, with Isaac Henry serving as the only uncapped player following an injury to Len Ikitau.

teams.heading: Ma’a Nonu signs short-term deal with the Sharks in South Africa
teams.body: All Blacks legend Ma’a Nonu is set to continue his career in Durban after confirming a short-term move to the Sharks. The 44-year-old double World Cup winner joins the franchise following a successful tenure at RC Toulon. Sources indicate the veteran midfielder will focus on a mentorship role, specifically tasked with guiding young centres Jurenzo Julius and Ethan Hooker. Nonu’s arrival is expected to bolster the club's leadership and culture as part of their ongoing high-performance restructuring.
